title: 第399章 神兽外交与议会转向第398章 解围之战与幸存者
lines: 天罗城救援归来后石青璇没有闲着。她每天一早带着青鸾、麒麟幼崽和几只灵雀走访轩辕城周边的村落和灵田。
她没有做什么惊天动地的大事，只是带着神兽们走了一圈又一圈。
麒麟幼崽走累了就在灵田边的树荫下翻肚皮睡觉，青鸾蹲在屋檐上看灵农们收灵禾，三只灵雀在村头的老井边轮流啄井台上的水珠。
但神兽们走过的每一寸土地都在悄悄发生变化。
麒麟的远古祥瑞法则碎片的自然外溢会自动驱散残余浊气——不是强效净化，是一种极温和的“被阳光晒过的空气”式的薄层覆盖。浊气在麒麟方圆里许的范围内自然消散了大半。
灵田里的灵禾在这层薄薄祥瑞灵气的滋养下增产了明显一截。青鸾的凤族旁支灵力对灵田土壤中的微生物群有激活作用——翻土后的灵苗扎根速度比往年快了不少。
一个老灵农跪在自己那片刚被麒麟踏过的田埂上抱着麒麟幼崽哭了。
他的村子从前人口众多，现在剩不到原来的几分之一——年轻人要么死在边境，要么受不了灵田连年减产进城做苦力。
孙辈中最小的那个刚学会走路便没了父母，老灵农一个人把孙儿拉扯到这岁数。他一直跟邻居说“这村子再过几十来年就没了”。
今天他这块田里的灵禾穗比去年重了一截，他把麒麟幼崽抱在怀里时哭得说不出一句完整的话。
麒麟幼崽听不懂他那些具体的词语，但它歪着头舔了舔老农手上那道被灵禾叶片割了几十年的老茧疤痕。
石青璇在一旁看着，眼眶也红了。
她没有上前说任何安慰的话，只是蹲下来给老农的孙儿从怀中掏出几枚朱雀果干——她来上界后商秀珣用荒古灵果晒的零食。
类似的情景在几十个村子重复发生。东山那带的灵农开始自发地在村口给神兽们摆一碗清水或一小碟晒干的灵谷粒——不是供奉，是给过路的客人准备的零嘴。
麒麟幼崽路过时会把碟子里的灵谷舔干净，然后用角轻轻碰一下摆碟子那户人家的门框——大概是说“我收到了，谢了”。
民间舆论在极短时间内不可逆地转向了。
“神兽不是敌人，是帮手。”隐忍派和投降派此前一直挂在嘴边的“神兽危险论”在灵禾增产和老农眼泪面前完全失去了说服力。
那些投神派议员想把话题拉到“神族若质询如何回应”的层面上时，东山灵农们已经把附近各村的“接待外来神兽的基本礼貌条款”整理成一份民间自发的小手册，满页写的都是“麒麟幼崽喜欢吃什么”、“灵雀怕冷要留一盏灯”、“青鸾洗澡时溪水要无浊不能过烫”。
没有一行字关于议会。
石青璇带着使团走访了不知多少村子后民间自发形成了一个非正式的“神兽接待联络网”。
以东山老灵农赵老八牵头，召集附近的各灵农代表定期跟石青璇碰头——联名致信议会表示“反对任何排斥神兽的政策与任何试图驱离神兽使者的动议”。
信末盖了满满一页不同字迹写成的心声和署名——每一只按在署名上的红泥都是不同人亲手将拇指在印泥上压了压在信纸上留下指纹印记。
姬老把这份联名信批了三个字：“存档。公开。”
当灵田边的哭与笑、麒麟偶尔的翻肚皮打鼾以及青鸾在清晨第一声清幽的低鸣以一种更贴近真实生活的坦诚流入轩辕城各处时，议会的会场变得比往日安静了许多。
那些一直在说“神兽危险论”或“不可让神族不高兴”的嘴在见到这份印满红泥拇指印的厚厚联名信后忽然都像灌了过量的白开水一样淡了下去。
石青璇通过青鸾传信，请神农来轩辕城。
神农踏入轩辕城那一日，无名老道亲自走出了青铜塔。
无名老道数年以来从未离开过塔基一步。他不是不能出来，是他修的是时间——时间只能守着不动，不能走到前面去。但今天他走出塔门了。
他从青铜塔底层的暗弱阵纹光影中一步步走出来，踩在轩辕城中央广场那些被无数代人走磨得发亮的青石板上。鹤发被广场两侧的风轻轻吹起，灰袍上还带着塔内壁画上那些古字的淡薄阵纹余光。
神农拄着木杖从街道另一端走来，麻衣上还带着百兽禁地清晨露水的湿润气息，杖端沾着一点百兽禁地特有的浅红色泥土。
两个老人在中央广场上相隔几步停下了脚步。谁都没有先开口。周围围观的飞升者们自发退到广场边缘，把整片空地留给这两个各自守护了人族数万年的老人。
神农先笑了笑。他笑起来时满脸皱纹全部堆到眼角和鼻梁两侧，看不出苦与乐的分别。
“我在荒古遗域守了漫长岁月，守的是人族最后的退路。你在青铜塔守了漫长岁月，守的是人族最后的屏障。我们做的是一件事。”
无名老道那只常年闭着的右眼也睁了睁，嘴角极淡地动了一下。
他说他从塔上往南边看的时候总能望到一颗星特别亮，就一直知道神农还在。
“那颗星有时候偏南，有时候隐约偏东，但一直没灭。每次看到它亮着，就知道百兽禁地还有人在照看着那片最后的缓冲地带。”
两老携手转身，并肩走进青铜塔。
content_en:
Shi Qingxuan was not idle after returning from the rescue in Tianluo City. She visits the villages and spiritual fields around Xuanyuan City with Qingluan, Qilin cubs and a few sparrows every morning.
She didn't do anything earth-shattering, she just led the mythical beasts around and around.
When the unicorn cub got tired from walking, it would turn over and sleep under the shade of a tree beside the spiritual field. Qingluan squatted on the eaves to watch the spiritual farmers harvesting the spiritual crops. Three spiritual sparrows took turns pecking at the water drops on the platform of the old well at the head of the village.
But every inch of land that the mythical beasts walk on is quietly changing.
The natural overflow of Kirin's ancient auspicious law fragments will automatically disperse the residual turbidity - not a powerful purification, but an extremely mild "sun-baked air"-style thin layer covering. Most of the turbid air naturally dissipated within a few miles of Qilin.
The Linghe in the spiritual field increased significantly under the nourishment of this thin layer of auspicious spiritual energy. Qingluan's Feng Clan side branch spiritual power has an activating effect on the microorganisms in the soil of the spiritual field - the spiritual seedlings after turning the soil take root much faster than in previous years.
An old spiritual farmer knelt on the edge of his field that had just been stepped on by the unicorn and cried holding the unicorn cub in his arms.
His village used to have a large population, but now less than a fraction of its original size remains - young people either died on the border, or they couldn't bear the reduction in production in the spiritual fields year after year and went to work as coolies in the city.
The youngest of the grandchildren lost his parents just after he learned to walk. Old Linnong raised his grandson to this age by himself. He kept telling his neighbors that "this village will be gone in a few decades."
Today, the ears of Linghe in his field are heavier than last year. When he held the unicorn cub in his arms, he cried so hard that he couldn't say a complete sentence.
The Kirin cub couldn't understand his specific words, but it tilted its head and licked the callus scar on the old farmer's hand that had been cut by Linghe leaves for decades.
Shi Qingxuan looked on with red eyes.
She didn't come forward to say any words of comfort. She just knelt down and took out a few dried Suzaku fruits from her arms for the old farmer's grandson - snacks that Shang Xiuxun had dried with ancient spiritual fruits after she came to the upper world.
Similar scenes occurred repeatedly in dozens of villages. The spiritual farmers in the Dongshan area began to spontaneously place a bowl of water or a small plate of dried spiritual grains for the sacred beasts at the entrance of the village - not as an offering, but as snacks for passing guests.
When the unicorn cub passes by, he will lick the spirit grains in the dish clean, and then gently touch the door frame of the house where the dish is placed with his horn - probably to say "I received it, thank you."
Public opinion turned irreversibly in a very short period of time.
"Mythical beasts are not enemies, but helpers." The "danger theory of mythical beasts" that the forbearance and surrender factions have always talked about has completely lost its persuasiveness in the face of the increase in Linghe production and the tears of old farmers.
When the god-seeking councilors wanted to bring the topic to the level of "how to respond to questions from the gods," the Dongshan Spiritual Farmers had already compiled the "basic courtesy provisions for receiving foreign mythical beasts" from nearby villages into a small manual spontaneously written by the people. The pages were filled with "What do unicorn cubs like to eat?"
There is not a single line about Parliament.
Shi Qingxuan led the delegation to visit an unknown number of villages, and an informal "mythical beast reception network" was spontaneously formed among the people.
Zhao Laoba, an old spiritual farmer from Dongshan, took the lead and convened representatives from nearby spiritual farmers to meet with Shi Qingxuan regularly. They jointly sent a letter to the parliament stating that they "oppose any policy that excludes the sacred beasts and any motion that attempts to expel the messengers of the sacred beasts."
At the end of the letter, there is a page full of sentiments and signatures written in different handwritings - each red clay pressed on the signature is a different person's hand who pressed his thumb on the ink pad and left a fingerprint mark on the letter paper.
Mr. Ji approved the joint letter with three words: "Archive. Make it public."
When the crying and laughter beside the spiritual field, Qilin's occasional belly turning and snoring, and Qingluan's first quiet whisper in the morning flowed into Xuanyuan City with a frankness closer to real life, the parliament venue became much quieter than before.
Those who had been talking about "theory of the danger of mythical beasts" or "don't make the gods unhappy" suddenly stopped as if they had been given too much plain water after seeing this thick joint letter with red mud thumbprints.
Shi Qingxuan sent a message through Qingluan, asking Shennong to come to Xuanyuan City.
On the day when Shennong entered Xuanyuan City, the unknown Taoist walked out of the bronze tower himself.
The unknown veteran has never left the base of the tower for several years. It's not that he can't come out, it's that what he cultivates is time - time can only stand still and cannot move forward. But today he walked out of the tower door.
He walked out step by step from the dim light and shadow at the bottom of the bronze tower, stepping on the bluestone slabs in the central square of Xuanyuan City that had been polished by countless generations of walking. The crane's hair was gently blown by the wind on both sides of the square, and the faint patterns of the ancient characters on the murals in the tower were still visible on the gray robe.
Shen Nong walked from the other end of the street with a wooden staff. His linen clothes still carried the moist smell of morning dew in the Forbidden City, and the end of the stick was stained with a bit of the light red soil unique to the Forbidden City.
The two old men stopped a few steps apart in the central square. No one spoke first. The surrounding Ascended Ones spontaneously retreated to the edge of the square, leaving the entire open space to these two old men who had each guarded the human race for tens of thousands of years.
Shennong smiled first. When he smiled, all the wrinkles on his face reached the corners of his eyes and the sides of his nose, and he couldn't tell the difference between pain and happiness.
"I have been guarding the ancient ruins for a long time, guarding the last retreat of the human race. You have been guarding the Bronze Tower for a long time, guarding the last barrier of the human race. We are doing the same thing."
The nameless old Taoist's right eye, which had been closed all year round, also opened, and the corner of his mouth moved slightly.
He said that when he looked south from the tower, he could always see a particularly bright star, and he always knew that Shennong was still there.
